t: Where has the male axis failed?
key: Ask where the failure sits and what LH and FSH are doing: a failing testis raises them, a failing pituitary or hypothalamus leaves them low, a blocked duct leaves everything normal, and an outside androgen suppresses them.
items: Tubular dysgenesis with Leydig failure leaves testosterone low, so feedback is lost and LH and FSH are high.
Inflammation inside the tight tunica destroys tubules, so LH and FSH rise.
Cytotoxic drugs kill germ cells and often Leydig cells, producing a high FSH.
Heat damages germ cells, so tubule failure raises FSH and the testes are small.
GnRH neurons fail to migrate with the olfactory placode, so LH and FSH are low.
Prolactin suppresses GnRH pulses, giving low LH, FSH and testosterone.
Opioids suppress GnRH release centrally, causing opioid-induced androgen deficiency.
Iron deposition in the pituitary lowers gonadotropins, so testosterone falls with low LH and FSH.
The vas is cut, so sperm cannot enter the ejaculate, but testis size and FSH stay normal.
Congenital absence of the vas deferens
CFTR mutations cause CBAVD with low-volume, fructose-negative semen and a normal FSH.
A blocked duct stops seminal vesicle fluid, so volume is low and fructose is absent.
Negative feedback shuts off LH and FSH, so the testes shrink and sperm vanish.
Synthetic androgens suppress gonadotropins in the same way, giving atrophy and azoospermia.
Testosterone gel in a man wanting children
Even topical testosterone suppresses LH and FSH and lowers intratesticular testosterone.
